title: Audit a registration form
description: Inspect an everyday form for unclear labels, hidden errors and unnecessary fields.
steps: Choose a form you can safely inspect.
List three confusing interactions.
Propose one change and explain the user benefit.

title: Plan a cognitive walkthrough
description: Predict where a new user might struggle while completing a short interface task.
steps: Write a realistic task and its starting point.
Inspect each action for discoverability and feedback.
Record assumptions that need testing with users.

title: Write a usability test script
description: Create neutral instructions for observing task completion without coaching the participant.
steps: Choose one task with a clear completion condition.
Write a neutral task prompt and consent explanation.
List errors, completion time and comments to record.

title: Publish an error description
description: Explain how the error occured and how to recover.
steps: Select a nonconfidential error you encountered.
Describe why its wording helped or confused you.
Rewrite it with a concrete recovery action.

title: Check keyboard navigation
description: Evaluate whether an interface can be used with a keyboard and visible focus.
steps: Navigate a page with Tab and Shift+Tab.
Check whether focus is visible on every control.
Identify one action that cannot be completed easily.

title: Review meaningful labels
description: Examine whether form labels and button names communicate their purpose.
steps: Inspect labels on one small interface.
Check whether a label identifies the required input.
Propose a clearer label for one confusing control.

title: Plan an accessible chart alternative
description: Describe how a chart can provide a text or table alternative without losing its main meaning.
steps: Choose a chart you are permitted to inspect.
Write the main takeaway in plain language.
List the values an accessible alternative should contain.

title: Read about inclusive interaction needs
description: Outline how different sensory and motor needs can change interaction requirements.
steps: Select a scholarly accessibility article yourself.
Identify the users and barriers it discusses.
Write two design requirements supported by the article.

title: Practice Python dictionaries
description: Use a dictionary for reliable lookup of records by stable identifiers.
steps: Create three fictional records with unique IDs.
Build a dictionary keyed by each ID.
Demonstrate lookup and explain duplicate ID handling.

title: Validate a JSON input
description: Practice checking input types and bounds before processing a request.
steps: Define the expected fields for a small JSON object.
Reject a missing field and an invalid value.
Write a helpful message for each rejected input.

title: Write a focused unit test
description: Test a meaningful boundary case in a small Python function.
steps: Choose a function with a clear expected behavior.
Write one ordinary and one boundary test.
Run the tests and inspect any failure message.

title: Explore sparse vectors
description: Compare sparse and dense representations for documents with many absent terms.
steps: Create a tiny document collection.
Inspect the shape and nonzero count of its TF IDF matrix.
Explain when sparse storage reduces unnecessary memory use.

title: Compare recommendation approaches
description: Explain the differences between content based, collaborative and hybrid recommendation.
steps: Read one peer reviewed recommendation survey.
Summarize the input used by each approach.
Identify an appropriate approach for a new user with no history.

title: Inspect a text similarity score
description: Use a small example to understand TF IDF features and cosine similarity.
steps: Create three short item descriptions.
Compare their TF IDF vectors with cosine similarity.
Explain why a similarity score is not a probability of satisfaction.

title: Evaluate variety in a result list
description: Compare a relevance only ranking with a list that penalizes repeated content.
steps: Run the same preference profile with two variety settings.
Compare repeated topics and changed positions.
Explain one tradeoff between similarity and variety.

title: Design a cold start strategy
description: Plan how a recommender can help a new user without assuming a personal history.
steps: Describe the information available for a new user.
Choose a transparent starter strategy.
Explain how the user can correct the first suggestions.

title: Map consent in an AI interface
description: Decide which optional intelligent behaviors should require a visible user choice.
steps: Choose an optional AI behavior.
Write a clear consent label describing that behavior.
Explain how a user can turn it off or reset it.

title: Review recommendation bias
description: Examine how a small catalogue can limit whose interests are represented.
steps: List the topics represented in a catalogue.
Identify an interest that is missing.
Explain why adding varied items is different from proving fairness.

title: Check an AI explanation
description: Separate a persuasive explanation from evidence of the ranking mechanism.
steps: Choose a recommendation with a visible explanation.
Find the item features supporting the explanation.
Record any claim that cannot be verified from those features.

title: Draft a data minimization plan
description: Plan which preference fields are necessary and how long they should be retained.
steps: List the preference fields an app needs.
Remove a field that does not support the task.
Specify a reset and retention rule in plain language.

title: Outline a literature review
description: Turn a research question into a short outline organized by ideas rather than articles.
steps: Write one focused research question.
Create three themes related to the question.
Place candidate sources under the themes they support.

title: Compare scholarly claims
description: Assess whether two articles support the same claim under similar conditions.
steps: Select two peer reviewed articles yourself.
Compare their participants, tasks and limitations.
Write one claim that the evidence can support.

title: Review an APA reference
description: Check whether a journal reference includes the verified authors, year, title and DOI.
steps: Open the publisher record for a journal article.
Compare it with your reference entry.
Correct any mismatch in author order, year or DOI.

title: Plan a research reflection
description: Connect a technical design choice to your own observations without inventing results.
steps: Choose one design decision you can explain.
Separate completed actions from proposed evaluation.
Describe one limitation and a concrete next step.
